sections.executive_summary:
Maryland does not issue a separate "non-medical home care" license. Any business that employs or contracts with workers to provide a home health care service, including personal care aide help with activities of daily living, to an unrelated sick or disabled person for pay is a **Residential Service Agency (RSA)**. RSAs are licensed by the Maryland Department of Health's Office of Health Care Quality (OHCQ) under **COMAR 10.07.05** [S1][S4]. The same license is the entry ticket to Medicaid. Personal assistance under **Community First Choice (CFC)** and **Community Personal Assistance Services (CPAS)** may only be delivered by a licensed RSA that employs a registered nurse and enrolls with Medicaid as provider type 76 [S11][S49][S40]. Community Options waiver participants get their personal assistance through CFC [S51].

**The opportunity is real but the Medicaid margin is thin.** CFC served 18,400–19,100 people a month in FY 2026, at roughly $53–58 million in claims per full month [S22]. In CY 2025, 16,543 people were billed under the main personal assistance code, W5519 [S14]. The Community Options waiver registry still held 20,778 people on June 30, 2026 [S22]. On the price side, the agency rate has been **$6.3962 per 15 minutes ($25.58/hour)** since July 1, 2024. The state did not raise it in FY 2026 or FY 2027 [S9][S14][S15]. At Maryland's 25th-percentile aide wage of $17.06 [S16] plus payroll burden, about 83% of every Medicaid dollar goes to the aide. That leaves roughly $314 per client per month to cover the RN, office, insurance and owner pay. The market is also crowded: the state's Medicaid RSA listing shows 1,195 provider numbers, concentrated in Prince George's (374), Baltimore County (323) and Montgomery (152) [S42].

**What works in the model:** a mixed agency that uses Medicaid for volume and private pay for margin. Maryland's median private-pay rate for non-medical in-home care is $35/hour [S20], which leaves about $616 per private client per month after costs. At 90% of target census:

- A **100-client mixed agency (60% Medicaid / 40% private pay)** nets about **$11,800 a month (5.5% margin)**.
- A **60-client mixed agency (70/30)** nets about **$3,600 a month (2.8%)**.
- **Medicaid-only agencies** lose money at 30 and 60 clients and barely break even at 100.

Section 8 shows how sensitive these results are to aide wages. In Montgomery County, a mixed agency with 51+ employees and under 75% Medicaid revenue must pay at least $18.00 an hour, which cuts the 100-client result to about $5,500 a month [S21].

**Timing matters in late 2026.** Medicaid moved provider enrollment to the new **MPRIME** system on October 13, 2026. Complete new applications filed by December 31, 2026 can be backdated [S39]. Every Medicaid HCBS provider must file the annual HCBS Cost Survey or face payment suspension [S12], and the state has begun formal RSA compliance audits [S38].
sections.service_model:
### Who is served and what the service is
"Personal home care" in Maryland means hands-on help with **activities of daily living** (bathing, dressing, eating, mobility, toileting) and **instrumental activities** (meals, light housekeeping, shopping, errands) in the client's own home [S4]. Under CFC, personal assistance also covers delegated nursing tasks, help with self-administered medication, and tasks requiring judgment to protect the participant from harm [S36]. It excludes housekeeping unrelated to the participant, the cost of food, and escort or travel expenses [S57].

### The license: Residential Service Agency
COMAR defines an RSA as any non-governmental business that employs or contracts with individuals to provide at least one home health care service, for pay, to an unrelated sick or disabled person in that person's residence [S4]. Licensed home health agencies, hospices, hospitals and Medicaid personal care providers under the older programs are excluded [S4]. On the application, the applicant checks the services it will offer: nursing, home health aide, therapies, medical social services, dietary services, or durable medical equipment [S2].

Workforce rules follow the client's needs:
- An agency may send a **non-certified aide** only when the client does not need ADL help, when the supervising nurse judges there are no predictable adverse health consequences, or when the client signs a waiver of skilled services [S5].
- A **certified caregiver** (CNA or certified medication technician) is required when a client needs a certified caregiver for ADLs or needs medication administered [S5].
- Under CFC, an aide who administers medication must be a CMT, and one who performs other delegated nursing tasks must also be a CNA [S11].

### Payers and how money flows
1. **Private pay** (self-pay families and long-term care insurance reimbursement to the family). Rates are set by the agency. COMAR requires a written cost estimate, a statement of what the client will owe, and itemized bills on request [S48].
2. **Maryland Medicaid, fee-for-service:**
   - **CFC** (COMAR 10.09.84). Participants must meet an institutional level of care, be Medicaid-eligible and live at home [S35].
   - **CPAS** (COMAR 10.09.20), a separate state plan personal assistance program with the same agency conditions [S49].
   - **Community Options waiver** members, who receive personal assistance through CFC.

   A supports planner builds a plan of service that names the provider agency. OLTSS sets a service budget based on assessed need [S35][S57]. Aides clock in and out through **ISAS**, the state's telephonic EVV system. ISAS turns verified time into electronic claims automatically [S8][S10]; agencies are paid weekly [S46]. Payment goes directly from the Department to the agency under the published fee schedule [S8].
3. **Other payers** (VA community care, county programs, LTC insurance). These were not verified and are not modeled.

### Oversight structure
- **OHCQ** licenses RSAs, investigates complaints and may inspect announced or unannounced [S1][S3].
- **OLTSS and DPICC** oversee Medicaid participation. They use a progressive process: desk review and site visit, plan of correction, then suspension and payment withholds [S38].
- **Federal law** requires EVV for Medicaid personal care [S55]. Maryland meets that requirement with ISAS.
sections.licensing_pathway:
### Track 1 — Business formation
1. **Form the entity.** File LLC Articles of Organization with SDAT: $100, plus $50 to expedite [S29]. Get an EIN [S53] and an organizational NPI [S54].
2. **Keep the SDAT number in good standing.** From October 13, 2026, Medicaid will not accept an MPRIME application without an SDAT ID in good standing. MPRIME automatically suspends providers that fall out of good standing [S39]. The LLC annual report and personal property return costs $300 a year (per the 2024 Form 1 manual; confirm the current fee) and is due April 15 [S30].
3. **Get workers' compensation insurance** before hiring. It is mandatory for any Maryland employer with one or more employees [S26]. OHCQ requires proof with the license application [S2].

### Track 2 — OHCQ Residential Service Agency license
1. **Prepare the package.** The application (rev. 06/26/2026) requires [S2]:
   - a business plan with a 1-year operating budget, a marketing plan naming the populations served, and a detailed description of services;
   - an organizational chart;
   - policies and procedures under COMAR 10.07.05.08B (administration, personnel, patient care, informed consent, environment and safety) [S47];
   - an SDAT letter of good standing;
   - workers' compensation documentation.

   COMAR also requires ownership disclosure for owners of 25% or more, prior license history, criminal-charge disclosures, and proof the applicant is 21 or older [S3].
2. **Complete the worker-classification certification.** Under Health-General §19-4A-11, a person with authority over pay or employment practices must read the RSA-PCA Guidance Document and submit the online RSA Certification form. This is required both to obtain and to keep the license [S1][S2].
3. **Submit online.** Use OHCQ's "Submit a License Application" Smartsheet link. Handwritten applications are returned [S2].
4. **Fee.** COMAR 10.07.05.04 sets a nonrefundable **$1,000 fee for a 3-year license** and a $1,000 renewal fee [S3]. The current application says "There is no fee to apply" [S2]. Budget the $1,000 and confirm with OHCQ whether it is billed at issuance.
5. **Review.** OHCQ may inspect before deciding [S3]. It may approve, approve with conditions (such as a required management firm for up to 24 months, or a license term under 1 year), or deny [S3]. Neither COMAR nor the application sets a processing deadline. OHCQ holds an incomplete application for **180 days** and then closes it administratively [S2]. A license runs **3 years** from issuance [S3].
6. **Later changes.** Change of ownership requires 45 days' written notice and a new license application [S1]. Additional services, address, name and branch changes each have their own OHCQ forms [S1].

### Track 3 — Medicaid enrollment (only if serving CFC/CPAS)
1. **Enroll in MPRIME** as provider type 76 (Community Options / CFC / CPAS). PT 76 is a **high/moderate-risk** provider type [S40]. Federal screening rules for those risk levels include site visits and, for high-risk types, fingerprinting of owners; confirm with MDH which applies. New applications have been on hold since July 1, 2026. MPRIME opened October 13, 2026. A complete application filed by **December 31, 2026** can be backdated to the later of July 1, 2026 or the license issue date [S39].
2. **Application fee.** The CY 2026 federal application fee is $750 [S32]. Whether Maryland collects it for PT 76 was not confirmed.
3. **Meet the conditions of participation:**
   - "be licensed as a Residential Service Agency under COMAR 10.07.05 to provide Level Two or Level Three home care services" [S11]. COMAR 10.07.05 no longer defines levels; confirm with OLTSS which services must be checked on the OHCQ application (home health aide at minimum);
   - **employ an RN** who assesses each new participant, helps write worker instructions, delegates nursing tasks and trains aides;
   - run criminal history checks on all direct service workers, including nurses;
   - collect the participant's signature on services rendered at least monthly;
   - give 45 days' notice before closure, a sale or a move [S11].

   No provider or principal may have had a license action, Medicaid sanction or termination in the prior 24 months [S59][S38].
4. **Register for ISAS.** Set up agency administrator and billing roles and train aides on clock-in and clock-out [S46]. ISAS is the only way to bill personal assistance [S8].
5. **Get referrals.** Participants choose their agency during plan-of-service development with their supports planner. The agency must sign the plan of service [S35].

### Medicaid (CFC and CPAS): one statewide fee schedule
| Code | Service | Rate | Effective |
|---|---|---|---|
| W5519 (CFC) / W5527 (CPAS) | Personal assistance, agency | **$6.3962 per 15 min ($25.58/hr)** | July 1, 2024 |
| W5521 / W5528 | Shared attendant | $4.2597 per 15 min | July 1, 2024 |
| W5532 | Daily rate (>12 hrs/day) | $329.84 per day | July 1, 2024 |

Sources: [S9][S14].

**Rate trend.** The FY 2025 schedule raised rates 3% on July 1, 2024 [S9]. The FY 2026 budget proposed a further 1% LTSS increase, and the Department of Legislative Services recommended deleting it [S33]. The state's July 1, 2025 rate disclosure still lists $6.3962 [S14]. The FY 2027 budget "provides level rates for long-term services and supports providers" [S15]. As of June 29, 2026, MDH reported no personal care rate updates [S13]. COMAR still calls for 3% annual increases, but only "subject to the limitations of the State budget" [S8]. **Plan on $6.3962 with no automatic raise.**

**Billing mechanics** [S8][S10][S46]:
- Units are 15 minutes for up to 12 hours a day. Above 12 hours, the daily rate applies.
- Time is captured only through ISAS phone clock-in/out, verified by the participant's landline or a one-time-password device. ISAS generates the claims from verified clock-in data, and agencies are paid weekly [S46].
- ISAS automatically cuts hours above the plan-of-service authorization, and those hours are not paid.
- MDH's 2020 ISAS training sets a limit of 4 missing-time requests, due within 2 business days after month-end, and a Thursday–Wednesday billing week [S46]. Confirm the current limit and how it is counted with the ISAS Help Desk.
- Claims must be submitted within 12 months of the date of service [S10].
- Medicaid pays the lesser of the fee schedule or your usual-and-customary charge to the public. Do not post a private rate below $25.58/hour if you bill Medicaid.

**What is not billable.** The RSA's own RN assessments, supervision visits, and on-call work are overhead built into the rate. Nurse Monitoring (W5522, $31.5348 per 15 min) is a separate service. Its providers are designated by the Department under §1915(b)(4) [S37][S9].

**Rate pressure ahead.** Under HB 1142 and the federal Access Rule, MDH started the **HCBS Cost Survey** on July 1, 2026 to build a cost-based rate method [S12][S13]. Under the federal payment-adequacy rule, providers must spend at least 80% of Medicaid payments on direct-care worker compensation. MDH's 2024 report says compliance is enforced from July 9, 2030, with small-provider and hardship exemptions possible [S43]. At $17.06/hour plus burden, the modeled agency spends about 83%.

### Private pay
Maryland's 2025 median for non-medical in-home care is **$35/hour** [S20]. That is a statewide median of agency hourly rates, not a price ceiling. Montgomery County and other high-income areas generally support higher rates, but no county figure was verified. Private clients often buy short shifts. The model assumes 60 hours a month per private client (operator assumption — verify locally).

### Other payers (not modeled)
Long-term care insurance usually reimburses the policyholder, so the agency bills the family. VA Homemaker/Home Health Aide care is purchased through VA community care contracts. Neither rate was verified, so both are listed as not claimed.
sections.demand:
### Medicaid volume
- **CFC users:** 18,443 in July 2025, rising to 19,107 in February 2026. Total CFC cost ran about $53.6–57.7 million in each full month [S22].
- **Personal assistance specifically:** 16,543 beneficiaries billed under W5519 and 1,033 under CPAS W5527 in CY 2025 [S14].
- **Community Options waiver:** 3,879–3,944 enrollees a month in FY 2026 (July 2025–March 2026; 4,562 filled slots, preliminary) against 4,941 budgeted slots. CMS approved 7,500 slots beginning January 1, 2027, but the FY 2027 budget funds 4,988 [S22].
- **Registry:** 20,778 people on June 30, 2026, down 9.9% from 23,060 a year earlier. Of these, 13,493 are 65+, about 53% have active Medicaid, and about 805 new registrants join each month. MDH sends about 700 invitations a month, but only 26% apply and 13% of applications ended in enrollment in FY 2026 [S22]. For a provider, the CFC state plan program is the more reliable volume source than waiver slots.

### Referral sources
CFC/CO applicants enter through **Maryland Access Point** (1-844-MAP-LINK) [S50]. Participants pick their personal assistance agency with their **supports planner**, and the plan of service names that agency [S35]. Practical referral channels are:
- supports planning agencies and local MAP sites;
- hospital and nursing-facility discharge planners (CFC also covers transitions from institutions) [S35];
- area agencies on aging;
- for private pay: physicians, elder-law attorneys, senior living communities and online search.

### Supply and competition
The state's Medicaid RSA listing (May 2026) shows **1,195 distinct provider numbers**. The heaviest counts are Prince George's (374), Baltimore County (323), Montgomery (152), Baltimore City (about 90), Anne Arundel (70) and Howard (58). Western Maryland and the Eastern Shore have only single digits per county [S42]. A new Medicaid agency in Prince George's or Baltimore County competes with hundreds of others for the same supports-planner referrals. Rural counties have fewer competitors but also fewer participants and longer drive times.

### Workforce supply
In 2024 Maryland had 6.15 home health and personal care aides per 1,000 residents, against 12.03 nationally, 7.00 in Virginia and 18.55 in Pennsylvania (MDH/Hilltop analysis of BLS data) [S58]. A thin aide pool means recruiting, not client demand, is often what limits growth.
sections.market_conditions:
### Wages (BLS OEWS May 2025)
| Role | Maryland 25th pct | Median | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| Home health & personal care aides | $17.06 | $18.29 | [S16] |
| Registered nurses | $40.26 | $47.98 | [S17] |
| Office supervisors (director proxy) | $28.21 | $35.64 ($74,140) | [S18] |
| Medical secretaries (scheduler/billing) | $20.84 | $23.00 ($47,850) | [S19] |
| Medical & health services managers | $48.66 ($101,200) | $63.37 | [S34] |

Aide pay in the Baltimore and Washington metro areas is close to the state figure (medians $18.10 and $18.52) [S16]. Maryland's 10th-percentile aide wage, $15.16, sits just above the **$15.00 state minimum wage** [S21].

**Local minimums** (from July 1, 2026) [S21]:
- **Howard County:** $16.00.
- **Montgomery County:** $18.00 for large employers, $16.50 for mid-size employers, $15.95 for small employers. A home care provider with 11+ employees falls in the $16.50 mid-size tier only if it receives at least 75% of its gross revenue from state and federal Medicaid programs.
- The modeled Medicaid aide wage of $17.06 clears every floor except Montgomery County for agencies under 75% Medicaid revenue with 51+ employees. The Medicaid-only configurations qualify for $16.50. The mixed configurations do not: the default 100-client mixed agency earns about 65% of revenue from Medicaid and the 60-client mixed agency about 74%. A mixed or private-pay Montgomery agency with 51+ employees must pay at least $18.00 to all aides.

### Pricing
- **Medicaid:** $25.58/hour, unchanged since July 2024 [S9][S14][S15].
- **Private pay:** $35/hour state median [S20].

The roughly $9.40/hour gap between the two is why the profitable configurations all carry private-pay clients.

### Supply
1,195 Medicaid RSA provider numbers are concentrated in the central and Capital-region counties [S42]. No official count of all licensed RSAs, Medicaid and private, was found.

### Trends to watch
1. **Rate setting may change.** MDH is collecting cost data to move to a cost-based method; results go to the IPAG in 2027 [S12][S13].
2. **Program integrity is tightening.** RSA compliance audits began in 2026 (non-responders are suspended after three outreach attempts) [S38]. MPRIME checks SDAT standing automatically, and organizational licenses must be uploaded by March 31, 2027 [S39].
3. **Federal H.R. 1 changes.** Immigrant eligibility narrows October 1, 2026, and retroactive coverage shrinks to 1–2 months from January 1, 2027 [S44]. Most CFC participants are older adults or people with disabilities, so the expansion-adult work requirements matter less for this market. Shorter retroactive coverage does raise the risk of serving clients before eligibility is confirmed.
sections.financial_narrative:
### How the P&L is built
The unit is one **active client**. Capacity is the census the office team is sized for. The 90% default occupancy is the share of that census actually billing its authorized hours in a month (operator assumption).

**Revenue per client per month:**
- **Medicaid client:** 100 authorized hours = 400 units × $6.3962 = **$2,558.48** [S9]. Maryland does not publish average authorized hours, so the 100 hours is an operator assumption. FY 2026 CFC spending averaged about $3,000 per user per month across all CFC services [S22], which caps personal assistance at about 119 hours.
- **Private-pay client:** 60 hours × $35 = **$2,100** [S20]. The hours are an operator assumption.

**Direct labor** scales with census. Aides are paid for 105 hours per 100 billed, allowing 5% for travel between clients and in-service time (operator estimate):
- Medicaid aides: Maryland 25th percentile, **$17.06** [S16].
- Private-pay aides: median, **$18.29** [S16].
- RN: **1.0 hour per client per month** at $47.98 [S17]. This covers COMAR supervision visits every 3–4 months, new-client assessments, delegation and documentation [S7]. The hours are an operator estimate.

**Payroll burden is 19%:**
- employer FICA 7.65% [S24];
- Maryland UI and FUTA, about 1.35% (new-employer UI is 1.0–2.6% on the first $8,500 [S25]);
- workers' compensation, 4% (mandatory [S26]; the rate is an operator estimate);
- sick and safe leave, about 3.3% [S27];
- FAMLI employer share, 0.45% from 2027 [S28];
- other benefits, about 2% (operator estimate).

**Fixed costs:**
- A salaried director, using Maryland's median office supervisor wage of **$74,140** as a proxy [S18], or a **$101,200** administrator at 100 clients [S34]. COMAR sets no administrator credential.
- A scheduler/ISAS billing coordinator at $47,850 per FTE [S19].
- An 800 sq ft office (1,200 sq ft at 100 clients) at $26.78/sq ft/yr (secondary source [S23]).
- The RSA license, $1,000 per 3 years [S3], and the SDAT annual report, $300 [S30].
- A 24/7 on-call stipend (COMAR 10.07.05.12G [S7]).
- Insurance, software, accounting (including the HCBS Cost Survey [S12]), marketing and utilities, all labeled operator estimates.

**Per-client costs:** aide mileage between clients at the 2026 IRS rate [S31], plus training, background checks and supplies (operator estimates).

### Per-client economics
- **Medicaid client:** aide labor plus burden ($2,131.65) takes 83% of revenue. After the RN ($57.10) and per-client costs ($55.38), **$314 a month** is left toward overhead.
- **Private-pay client:** aide labor plus burden is $1,371.21, leaving **$616 a month**.

### Results at 90% of target census
| Configuration | Net / month | Margin | Break-even clients |
|---|---|---|---|
| 100 clients, 60% Medicaid / 40% private | **+$11,806** | 5.5% | 63 |
| 60 clients, 70% Medicaid / 30% private | **+$3,632** | 2.8% | 45 |
| 100 clients, Medicaid only | +$2,035 | 0.9% | 84 |
| 30 clients, private only | +$178 | 0.3% | 27 |
| 60 clients, Medicaid only | −$810 | −0.6% | 57 |
| 30 clients, Medicaid only | −$6,775 | −9.8% | 49 |

At 80% census, the 100-client mixed agency still makes about $7,450 a month and the 60-client mixed agency about $1,200. The Medicaid-only 100-client agency turns negative (−$1,108).

### Sensitivity
- **Aide wage.** This is the decisive input. If Medicaid aides must be paid the state median of **$18.29** instead of $17.06:
  - the 100-client mixed agency falls to +$3,507 (1.6%);
  - the 60-client mixed agency falls to −$2,178;
  - the 100-client Medicaid-only agency falls to −$11,797.

  The 60-client mixed agency breaks even at a Medicaid aide wage of about **$17.83**.
- **Montgomery County wage floor.** The $16.50 tier applies only if at least 75% of gross revenue comes from Medicaid [S21]. A mixed agency like the default (about 65% Medicaid revenue) with 51+ employees must pay $18.00 in Montgomery County. At $18.00 for Medicaid aides:
  - the 100-client mixed agency nets about **+$5,464** a month (2.6%, break-even 75 clients; about +$1,817 at 80% census);
  - the 60-client mixed agency nets about **−$808** (break-even 56.5 clients).

  The Medicaid-only configurations qualify for $16.50 and are unaffected.
- **Medicaid rate.** The 60-client Medicaid-only agency breaks even at about **$6.43 per 15 minutes**, about 0.6% above today's rate.
- **Private price.** If private pay brings $32/hour instead of $35, the 60-client mixed agency drops to +$716 and the 30-client private agency to −$4,682.
- **RN time.** At 1.5 RN hours per client per month, the 100-client mixed agency earns +$9,237.
- **Workers' comp.** At a 7% premium, the 100-client mixed agency earns +$7,038.

### Cash needs
Startup costs run about $14,000–$35,000, depending on size. The real cash need is the ramp-up loss while census builds. The P&L generator computes this from the ramp. At the modeled ramp it is roughly $114,000 for the 60-client mixed agency and $188,000 for the 100-client mixed agency, before startup costs.
sections.risks:
1. **Flat Medicaid rate and rising wages.** The CFC/CPAS rate has been $6.3962 since July 2024 and was held level for FY 2027 [S9][S15]. Every $1/hour of aide pay costs a Medicaid agency about $125 per 100-hour client per month after burden. At the state median aide wage ($18.29), every Medicaid-heavy configuration loses money [S16].
2. **Local minimum wages.** Montgomery County's minimum rises each July 1 with CPI-W. The $16.50 tier (from July 1, 2026) applies to home care providers with 11+ employees only if at least 75% of gross revenue comes from Medicaid; other employers with 51+ employees pay $18.00 [S21]. Howard County is $16.00 [S21]. A mixed agency like the default (about 65% Medicaid revenue) with 51+ employees must pay $18.00 in Montgomery County. At $18.00 for Medicaid aides, the 100-client mixed agency nets about +$5,464 a month (2.6%, break-even 75 clients; about +$1,817 at 80% census) and the 60-client mixed agency about −$808 (break-even 56.5 clients).
3. **ISAS billing leakage.** Hours above the plan of service are cut automatically and not paid. MDH's 2020 ISAS training limits missing-time requests to 4 (confirm the current rule with the ISAS Help Desk) [S46], and claims must be submitted within 12 months of service [S10]. Weak clock-in discipline turns directly into unpaid payroll.
4. **Compliance and suspension risk.** Payment can be suspended for:
   - missing the HCBS Cost Survey (deadline December 31, 2026) [S12];
   - not answering an RSA audit (suspension after three outreach attempts) [S38];
   - letting SDAT good standing lapse [S39];
   - not uploading a current license in MPRIME by March 31, 2027 [S39].

   A sanction also bars the owners from participating for 24 months [S59][S38].
5. **Saturated central-county markets.** Prince George's and Baltimore County together list about 700 Medicaid RSAs [S42]. Referrals depend on supports planners and participant choice, so a new agency must differentiate on reliability and language capacity.
6. **Workforce scarcity and turnover.** Maryland has about half the national aide density [S58]. A worker-organization member told the IPAG that only about 14% of RSAs report providing paid sick leave, but the underlying survey is unverified [S52]. Paid sick leave is mandatory at 15+ employees [S27].
7. **Federal policy changes.** H.R. 1 narrows Medicaid eligibility for some immigrants (October 1, 2026) and shortens retroactive coverage (January 1, 2027) [S44]. The federal 80% direct-care spending standard (enforced from July 2030 per MDH) limits how much of the rate can go to overhead [S43].
8. **Enrollment timing.** New Medicaid applications were held from July 1 to October 13, 2026. The MPRIME backdate applies only to complete applications filed by December 31, 2026 [S39].
9. **Unverified operator assumptions.** The 100 Medicaid and 60 private hours per client, 90% delivery, 5% non-billable aide time, 1.0 RN hour per client, insurance and the workers' comp rate are all operator estimates. See the sensitivity results in Section 8.
sections.recommendations:
1. **Build a mixed-payer agency from day one.** Medicaid CFC/CPAS gives volume and steady referrals. Private pay at around $35/hour [S20] produces most of the margin. Target at least 30% private-pay clients, and aim for about 100 active clients by year two. That is the only modeled size with a comfortable cushion: +$11,800 a month at 90% census, and still positive at 80%.
2. **Sequence the licenses to catch the MPRIME backdate.** Form the LLC and get SDAT good standing, then obtain workers' comp [S26][S29]. File the OHCQ RSA application with complete policies [S2], and complete the worker-classification certification [S1]. Once the license issues, file a complete MPRIME PT 76 application. If the license issues in 2026, file by **December 31, 2026** to get the backdate [S39].
3. **Hire or contract the RN early.** The RN must be employed for CFC/CPAS [S11] and drives client onboarding (assessments and plans of care) [S7]. A part-time RN at about 1 hour per client per month is enough at small scale.
4. **Engineer ISAS compliance.** Train every aide on clock-in and clock-out before the first shift [S46]. Have the coordinator review exceptions daily, and match schedules to plan-of-service hours [S10]. Unbilled hours are the fastest way to lose the thin Medicaid margin.
5. **Pay competitively but deliberately.** At $25.58/hour, a Medicaid aide wage above about $17.80 erases the 60-client mixed model's profit. Pay private-pay aides more, since private revenue supports it. Use shared-attendant authorizations ($4.2597 per 15 minutes per participant [S9]) where two participants share a home.
6. **Pick geography on purpose.** Central counties have the most participants and the most competitors [S42]. Under-served counties may offer easier supports-planner relationships but longer drive times. Check Montgomery and Howard wage floors before choosing [S21]. In Montgomery County, the $16.50 home care tier requires at least 75% of gross revenue from Medicaid; a mixed agency with 51+ employees below that share pays $18.00, which roughly halves the 100-client mixed result and puts the 60-client mixed agency at a loss [S21].
7. **Calendar the compliance deadlines.**
   - HCBS Cost Survey: December 31 each year [S12].
   - RSA wage report to the Department of Labor: September 1 [S43].
   - SDAT annual report: April 15 [S30].
   - RSA license renewal: every 3 years [S3].
   - MPRIME license upload: by March 31, 2027 [S39].
   - FAMLI contributions: from January 1, 2027 [S28].
8. **Capitalize for the ramp.** Plan roughly $130,000–$225,000 of total cash (startup plus ramp-up losses), depending on target size.

checklist.task: Form a Maryland LLC (or corporation) with SDAT
checklist.instructions: File Articles of Organization through Maryland Business Express. Fee $100 for a domestic LLC, plus $50 to expedite (7–10 business days). Non-expedited filings can take 4–6 weeks.

checklist.task: Confirm the SDAT ID is in good standing and get a good-standing letter
checklist.instructions: OHCQ requires an SDAT letter of good standing with the RSA application. From Oct 13, 2026, Medicaid's MPRIME rejects applications without an SDAT ID in good standing and auto-suspends providers that lose it.

checklist.task: Obtain an EIN from the IRS
checklist.instructions: Free online and issued immediately. Needed for payroll, banking, SDAT, NPI and MPRIME.

checklist.task: Obtain an organizational (Type 2) NPI
checklist.instructions: Apply free in NPPES. Required for Medicaid enrollment as PT 76.

checklist.task: Buy workers' compensation insurance before hiring anyone
checklist.instructions: Mandatory for every Maryland employer with one or more employees. Use any licensed carrier, including Chesapeake Employers' Insurance Company, Maryland's insurer of guaranteed market. The declaration page is an attachment to the RSA application.

checklist.task: Register for Maryland unemployment insurance and state withholding
checklist.instructions: New employers pay UI at 1.0%–2.6% on the first $8,500 per employee (2026, Table A).

checklist.task: Register with the FAMLI program and set up payroll deductions for Jan 1, 2027
checklist.instructions: Total rate 0.9% of wages. Employers may withhold up to half; employers under 15 employees remit only 50% of the rate.

checklist.task: Set the minimum pay floor for your county
checklist.instructions: State $15.00; Howard County $16.00; Montgomery County $16.50 for home care providers with 11+ employees that receive at least 75% of gross revenue from Medicaid; otherwise $18.00 (51+ employees), $16.50 (11–50), $15.95 (10 or fewer), all from July 1, 2026. A mixed Medicaid/private agency under 75% Medicaid revenue with 51+ employees pays $18.00. Overtime after 40 hours.

checklist.task: Bind general/professional liability, non-owned auto and crime/fidelity coverage
checklist.instructions: COMAR 10.07.05 sets no liability minimum. Get broker quotes; private clients and referral partners often ask for certificates.

checklist.task: Lease a small office (≈800 sq ft)
checklist.instructions: Baltimore asking rents average about $26.78/sq ft/yr full-service (secondary source; verify). COMAR requires personnel records to be kept in the agency's business office.

checklist.phase: PHASE 2 — OHCQ RESIDENTIAL SERVICE AGENCY LICENSE
checklist.task: Confirm your services fit the RSA definition and choose services on the application
checklist.instructions: RSA = business employing/contracting workers to provide at least one home health care service (e.g., home health aide/personal care) to an unrelated sick or disabled person at home. Check the services you will offer (e.g., home health aide; nursing if you will provide skilled nursing).

checklist.phase: PHASE 2 — OHCQ RESIDENTIAL SERVICE AGENCY LICENSE
checklist.task: Download the current RSA License Application (rev. 06/26/2026)
checklist.instructions: From the OHCQ RSA page. Type the form; handwritten applications are returned.

checklist.phase: PHASE 2 — OHCQ RESIDENTIAL SERVICE AGENCY LICENSE
checklist.task: Write the business plan
checklist.instructions: Must include a 1-year operating budget, a marketing plan naming the populations served, and a detailed description of services.

checklist.phase: PHASE 2 — OHCQ RESIDENTIAL SERVICE AGENCY LICENSE
checklist.task: Prepare the policies and procedures manual (COMAR 10.07.05.08B)
checklist.instructions: Cover administration (scope, admission criteria, pre-admission assessment, billing, QA, clinical management); personnel (job descriptions, skill assessments, health requirements); patient care (medication, monitoring frequency); informed consent; environment and safety (infection control, emergency procedures).

checklist.phase: PHASE 2 — OHCQ RESIDENTIAL SERVICE AGENCY LICENSE
checklist.task: Prepare the organizational chart and governing authority structure
checklist.instructions: The governing authority must meet at least annually with management and keep minutes.

checklist.phase: PHASE 2 — OHCQ RESIDENTIAL SERVICE AGENCY LICENSE
checklist.task: Prepare ownership and history disclosures
checklist.instructions: Identify every owner with 25% or more; disclose prior license denials, suspensions or revocations, criminal charges, and Medicare/Medicaid violations; applicant must be 21+. A suspension or revocation bars ownership for 10 years.

checklist.phase: PHASE 2 — OHCQ RESIDENTIAL SERVICE AGENCY LICENSE
checklist.task: Complete the RSA worker-classification certification (Health-General §19-4A-11)
checklist.instructions: The person who controls pay and employment practices reads the RSA-PCA Guidance Document and submits the online RSA Certification form. Required to get and keep the license. Classify aides as W-2 employees unless counsel advises otherwise.

checklist.phase: PHASE 2 — OHCQ RESIDENTIAL SERVICE AGENCY LICENSE
checklist.task: Submit the application through OHCQ's 'Submit a License Application' Smartsheet form
checklist.instructions: Upload all attachments. OHCQ holds an incomplete application for 180 days from first receipt, then closes it.

checklist.phase: PHASE 2 — OHCQ RESIDENTIAL SERVICE AGENCY LICENSE
checklist.task: Budget the $1,000 three-year license fee
checklist.instructions: COMAR 10.07.05.04A(2)(k) sets a nonrefundable $1,000 fee for a 3-year license. The 2026 application says no fee is due to apply; confirm with OHCQ whether the fee is billed at issuance.

checklist.phase: PHASE 2 — OHCQ RESIDENTIAL SERVICE AGENCY LICENSE
checklist.task: Prepare for a possible pre-licensure inspection
checklist.instructions: OHCQ may make an announced or unannounced on-site inspection before deciding. Each additional pre-licensure visit caused by noncompliance costs $250.

checklist.phase: PHASE 2 — OHCQ RESIDENTIAL SERVICE AGENCY LICENSE
checklist.task: Respond to any conditional approval terms
checklist.instructions: The Secretary may approve conditionally, e.g., requiring an approved management firm (max 24 months) or a license term under 1 year.

checklist.task: Hire or contract a Maryland-licensed RN (employ the RN if you will serve CFC/CPAS)
checklist.instructions: The RN assesses new clients who need ADL help, develops the plan of care, decides whether a CNA is needed, and trains aides. CFC/CPAS require the agency to employ the RN.

checklist.task: Build the RN supervision schedule
checklist.instructions: On-site supervision at least every 45 days if staff administer medication, every 3 months if staff assist with self-administration, every 4 months otherwise. Document every visit.

checklist.task: Set up 24/7 on-call with a 1-hour response and a call log
checklist.instructions: Give clients written on-call procedures and the phone number.

checklist.task: Implement the aide screening process
checklist.instructions: State criminal history (or private) check, license/certification verification, TB and health screen, references, employment history, I-9, identity, in-person interview, skills demonstration before the first client.

checklist.task: Decide which clients need certified aides (CNA/CMT)
checklist.instructions: Certified caregivers are required for clients who need a certified caregiver for ADLs or medication administration. Non-certified aides only where COMAR allows (no ADL need, RN judgment, or a signed waiver of skilled services). Under CFC, aides administering medication must be CMTs, and those doing other delegated tasks must be CNAs.

checklist.task: Build the aide training program
checklist.instructions: Personal care skills with supervised practice, when to call the RN, record keeping, ethics and confidentiality, CPR, infection control, abuse and neglect prevention. Keep training records in each personnel file.

checklist.task: If using an outside trainer, confirm OHCQ approval first
checklist.instructions: Outside trainers must be approved in writing by OHCQ before training (Outside Trainer checklist and Smartsheet form).

checklist.task: Create client rights packet and intake forms
checklist.instructions: Cost estimate, statement of private-pay responsibility, itemized billing on request, caregiver and supervisor names, 24/7 number, subcontract disclosure, rights, OHCQ/APS complaint access, advance directive information. Include the OHCQ hotline 800-492-6005.

checklist.task: Create informed-consent and waiver-of-skilled-services forms
checklist.instructions: Needed when a capable client declines recommended certified or skilled care.

checklist.task: Write the earned sick and safe leave policy
checklist.instructions: 1 hour per 30 hours worked (or front-load), 40-hour annual accrual, 64-hour cap. Paid at 15+ employees, unpaid below.

checklist.task: Set up private-pay scheduling/billing software and price list
checklist.instructions: Posted private rates should not be below the Medicaid rate if you bill Medicaid (Medicaid pays the lesser of usual-and-customary or the fee schedule). Maryland median private rate is $35/hour.

checklist.task: Create an MPRIME account and file a PT 76 application (Community Options / CFC / CPAS)
checklist.instructions: MPRIME launched Oct 13, 2026 at www.mprime.health.maryland.gov. ePREP logins do not transfer. File a complete application by Dec 31, 2026 to be backdated to the later of July 1, 2026 or your license date.

checklist.task: Prepare for high/moderate-risk screening
checklist.instructions: PT 76 is a high/moderate-risk provider type. Expect enhanced screening of owners and a possible site visit; confirm requirements with Provider Services (1-844-463-7768).

checklist.task: Budget for a possible $750 enrollment application fee
checklist.instructions: The CY 2026 federal fee is $750. Ask MPRIME support whether it applies to PT 76.

checklist.task: Confirm owners and principals meet the 24-month clean-history rule
checklist.instructions: No license suspension or revocation, Medicaid suspension or sanction, disciplinary action, health and safety deficiency citation, or agreement termination in the past 24 months.

checklist.task: Sign the provider agreement and meet CFC/CPAS conditions
checklist.instructions: RSA license 'to provide Level Two or Level Three home care services' (COMAR 10.07.05 no longer defines levels; confirm with OLTSS which services to check on the OHCQ application, home health aide at minimum); employed RN; aides accept instruction from the participant, nurse monitor, physician or MDH; monthly participant signature verifying services; 45-day notice of closure, sale or move; criminal checks on all direct workers.

checklist.task: Register the agency in ISAS and set up admin and billing users
checklist.instructions: Call the ISAS Help Desk (1-855-463-5877, from 2020 training; confirm current). Up to 5 admin and 5 billing roles. Aides cannot log into the portal.

checklist.task: Train every aide on ISAS clock-in and clock-out
checklist.instructions: Call at the start and end of every shift. Visits are verified by the participant's primary landline or an OTP device; the aide's phone number must never match the client's. Clocking in and out is the only way to bill personal assistance.

checklist.task: Set up the missing-time and exception workflow
checklist.instructions: Per MDH's 2020 ISAS training: a limit of 4 missing-time requests, each with a detailed reason, due within 2 business days after month end; hours above the plan of service are reduced automatically and unpaid; billing week runs Thursday to Wednesday. Confirm current policy with the ISAS Help Desk (855-463-5877).

checklist.task: Verify each participant's Medicaid eligibility monthly
checklist.instructions: Required at the start of every month services are provided.

checklist.task: Set up incident reporting
checklist.instructions: Report incidents and complaints within 24 hours and submit the written form within 7 days. Report suspected abuse or neglect to the local department of social services immediately.

checklist.task: Introduce the agency to supports planning agencies and MAP sites
checklist.instructions: Participants choose their personal assistance agency during plan-of-service development, and the plan must name and be signed by your agency. MAP: 1-844-MAP-LINK.

checklist.task: Market to discharge planners and private-pay referral sources
checklist.instructions: CFC covers participants transitioning from institutions. Private-pay referrals come from physicians, senior communities and elder-law attorneys.

checklist.task: RN assessment and plan of care before services
checklist.instructions: Assess before services start (within 48 hours for listed skilled needs). The plan states services, frequency, who provides them, goals and safety measures.

checklist.task: Match schedules to authorized plan-of-service hours
checklist.instructions: Do not schedule more hours than authorized. Use shared-attendant codes (W5521/W5528, $4.2597/15 min) when two participants share an aide.

checklist.task: Bill private clients with itemized statements

checklist.instructions: Aides are paid before cash arrives. Keep a payroll float (see the P&L ramp-up deficit).

checklist.task: File the annual HCBS Cost Survey
checklist.instructions: Required for every Medicaid-enrolled HCBS provider that billed in the reporting year. The FY 2026 survey is due Dec 31, 2026. Non-filers are suspended from Jan 1, 2027 until filed.

checklist.task: Upload your RSA license to MPRIME before March 31, 2027 and after every renewal
checklist.instructions: Expired licenses on file trigger automatic suspension (Status 54) from April 1, 2027.

checklist.task: Renew the RSA license every 3 years
checklist.instructions: Renewal application, $1,000 fee, changed policies (complaints, client evaluation), current professional licenses of all employees, annual data collection survey.

checklist.task: File the annual RSA personal care aide wage report with the Department of Labor
checklist.instructions: By September 1 each year: average, highest and lowest PCA wage rates (HB 189/SB 371 of 2024).

checklist.task: File the SDAT annual report and personal property return
checklist.instructions: $300 for an LLC, due April 15. Lapses suspend Medicaid participation through MPRIME's SDAT interface. Fee per the 2024 Form 1 manual ($300); confirm the current fee with SDAT.

checklist.task: Respond to RSA compliance audits within deadlines
checklist.instructions: Non-responders are suspended after three outreach attempts. Respond to a plan of correction within 15 calendar days. Repeat findings within 6 months can bring sanctions.

checklist.task: Keep Medicaid service records for 6 years
checklist.instructions: Dates and hours of services, monthly participant signatures, ISAS records.

checklist.task: Give 45 days' notice before any change of ownership, location, name, tax ID or closure
checklist.instructions: Notify OHCQ (new owner applies for a new license) and Medicaid; include the client transition plan.

checklist.task: Hold annual governing-authority meeting with minutes
checklist.instructions: Review policies with management at least annually.

checklist.task: Reassess each client at least annually and on significant change
checklist.instructions: Within 48 hours for listed skilled changes, or within 7 days if the RN documents that 48 hours is not needed.

checklist.task: Re-check local minimum wages every July 1
checklist.instructions: Montgomery County rates change each July 1 with CPI-W.

checklist.task: Monitor direct-care spending share against the federal 80% standard
checklist.instructions: MDH's cost survey will measure the share of Medicaid payments spent on direct-care worker pay. Federal compliance applies from July 9, 2030 per MDH's 2024 report.

corrections_vs_previous: No previous Maryland Personal Home Care market research report or licensing checklist was found in the Drive asset folder (read-only search for Maryland / home care / Residential Service Agency, October 13, 2026). Nothing could be carried over, and every figure here was researched fresh.

The only Maryland checklists in Drive are DDA (Developmental Disabilities Administration) provider applications under COMAR 10.22, for Supported Living and Personal Supports. Do not reuse them for this bundle. Non-medical home care and CFC/CPAS personal assistance need an OHCQ Residential Service Agency license (COMAR 10.07.05) plus Medicaid PT 76 enrollment (COMAR 10.09.84.06 / 10.09.20.05), not DDA approval.

Any material that still points applicants to ePREP is out of date. Maryland Medicaid replaced ePREP with MPRIME on October 13, 2026, and ePREP documents became inaccessible October 1, 2026 [S39][S41].
Any template that assumes the CFC rate rises 3% each July is wrong for FY 2026 and FY 2027. The rate has been $6.3962 per 15 minutes since July 1, 2024 [S9][S14][S15].

Any material describing an 'Independent Personal Assistance provider' route for a start-up is out of date. CFC/CPAS no longer accept those applications [S45]; personal assistance must go through a licensed RSA.
